ai.description: This frog reaches 4–6 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct golden-yellow crossband across the back and dark limb bars. It features a pointed snout and long, slender toes with prominent discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Odorrana yunnanensis* is best distinguished by the distinct, bright golden-yellow crossband pattern across its back, which is absent in other similar Indian *Odorrana* species.
ai.habitat: *Odorrana yunnanensis* inhabits moist, subtropical evergreen forests and rocky stream banks at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters in the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Golden Crossband Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt for insects along the rocky banks of mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Odorrana yunnanensis* is an oviparous breeder that deposits eggs in water. It breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of pigmented eggs in streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Odorrana yunnanensis* is found in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland, inhabiting montane forests at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Golden Crossband Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "peep" notes, typically heard echoing near fast-flowing mountain streams in its forest habitat.
